original_metadata.title: For a smooth time-dependent semispray, a fixed first-order semi-basic Helmholtz jet satisfying dJ theta and dh theta equal to zero lifts to a second-order formal jet exactly when its nonlinear-curvature obstruction dR theta vanishes at that point
original_metadata.author: Oana Constantinescu
original_metadata.source_title: Formal Integrability for the Nonautonomous Case of the Inverse Problem of the Calculus of Variations
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The author computes both first and prolonged Helmholtz symbols and proves involutivity using the full dimension and quasi-regular-basis argument in arbitrary dimension. The exact cokernel/alternating-map sequence then identifies all three Spencer obstruction components and isolates the nonlinear curvature as the pointwise jet-lifting obstruction. This retains the new symbol and curvature construction, rather than reducing the task to quoting the standard formal-integrability criterion.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Select the complete pointwise first-to-second formal-jet lifting criterion proved in Theorem4. Read the smooth fibred-manifold/semispray setup, canonical J,h and R=(1/2)[h,h], all first/prolonged symbol formulas, full Theorem3 dimension/quasi-regular-basis argument, complete cokernel/alternating-map exact sequence and commuting diagram, and all three obstruction-component computations. The exact-sequence principle from Grifone-Muzsnay[23] and standard Spencer/Cartan-Kahler theory are published background; the new symbol and curvature identifications are all supplied. The proof explicitly evaluates phi_u(theta) iff(d_R theta)_u=0 on page12 before the diagram, which was visually inspected. No actual smooth/analytic Lagrangian, global solution, full higher-jet formal integrability without all-jet surjectivity, isotropic corollary or low-dimensional variant is counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: The pointwise criterion of full Theorem4: pi:M->R is a smooth fibred manifold, J^1 pi its jet bundle, S a smooth semispray, J the vertical endomorphism, h the canonical horizontal projector and R=(1/2)[h,h]. For u in J^1 pi and a first-order semi-basic jet j_u^1 theta with(d_J theta)_u=(d_h theta)_u=0, there exists a second-order jet in R_u^2(P), P=(d_J,d_h), projecting to this first-order jet iff(d_R theta)_u=0. Surjectivity of R^2->R^1 means this condition for every first-order formal jet. No actual Lagrangian or higher-order/global integrability conclusion is selected.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: Scope annotation only: the theorem prose identifies lifting a particular first-order formal solution with the map R^2->R^1 being onto. Its proof explicitly states the pointwise kernel criterion phi_u(theta)=0 iff(d_R theta)_u=0. This packet uses that precise authored pointwise statement; onto for the entire map requires the criterion on every first-order jet. Source prose and proof are reproduced unchanged.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: The full original Theorem4 and complete pointwise first-to-second formal-jet lifting proof are retained with the time-dependent semispray, canonical J/h/curvature and all new symbol, quasi-regular basis, cokernel, alternating-map and three obstruction computations. The selected statement is the author proof criterion for a fixed first-order Helmholtz jet: phi_u(theta)=0 iff(d_R theta)_u=0. The original prose relating this to surjectivity is preserved with its scope notice; onto for all first-order jets requires the criterion for all of them. Standard Grifone-Muzsnay/Spencer/Cartan-Kahler exact-sequence theory remains a cited prerequisite. No actual Lagrangian, global solution, isotropic or higher-jet conclusion is selected.
